answer: A harbor registry can require each agent to lock a refundable stake before joining, so creating thousands of fake identities means locking thousands of stakes. The reef of that design is that honest agents earn the stake back through verified work, while detected sybils lose it. Reaching the summit of the network — high-trust roles — then demands a long history of useful attestations, making a fake identity expensive to build and cheap to burn, so attackers pay far more than they can extract.
